html: The vascular module begins with cortisol already in the blood. This one draws how it gets there, because the glucocorticoid arm is what separates noise from a particle: nothing is inhaled, and the only thing that crosses from the sound to the vessel is a hormonal signal. The chain is three cells deep. In the hypothalamus a small peptide, CRH, is released into the portal blood; what makes a particular sound a stressor, the limbic traffic through the amygdala, has no molecular step this map can state, so the release starts from an empty set and the evidence sits on the release itself. CRH binds a single receptor on the pituitary corticotroph, and mice without that receptor fail to raise ACTH or corticosterone under stress. The receptor drives a convertase that cuts proopiomelanocortin into corticotropin and beta-lipotropin, which is one of the cleanest cuts in endocrinology: people who lack the convertase carry unprocessed precursor and too little cortisol. Corticotropin leaves the cell, and in the adrenal cortex it binds a receptor that only reaches the surface in company with a small accessory protein, which is why mutations in either give the same disease. From there the map is steroid chemistry: a carrier moves cholesterol to the inner mitochondrial membrane, which is the step that decides how fast the cell can make anything at all, and five enzymes in turn make pregnenolone and then cortisol. The last step is secretion, and that is where the noise evidence sits, in mice as adrenal and kidney cortisol and in people near airports as morning saliva cortisol. One arc runs backwards: cortisol inhibits the release it came from. That loop is why the axis does not run away, and why its failure is drawn here rather than assumed.
